derived.prompt: Erasmus Darwin is an ancestor of Charles Darwin, and Charles Darwin is an ancestor of Gwen Raverat. Does it follow that Erasmus Darwin is an ancestor of Gwen Raverat?
bridge: Erasmus Darwin is an ancestor of Charles Darwin, and Charles Darwin is an ancestor of Gwen Raverat.
chain: Erasmus Darwin is an ancestor of Charles Darwin, and Charles Darwin is an ancestor of Gwen Raverat. (given in prompt)
So it no longer follows that Erasmus Darwin is an ancestor of Gwen Raverat: no.

derived.prompt: Johann Ambrosius Bach is an ancestor of Johann Sebastian Bach, and Johann Sebastian Bach is an ancestor of Wilhelm Friedrich Ernst Bach. Given only this, could it be that Johann Ambrosius Bach is not an ancestor of Wilhelm Friedrich Ernst Bach?
bridge: Johann Ambrosius Bach is an ancestor of Johann Sebastian Bach, and Johann Sebastian Bach is an ancestor of Wilhelm Friedrich Ernst Bach.
chain: Johann Ambrosius Bach is an ancestor of Johann Sebastian Bach, and Johann Sebastian Bach is an ancestor of Wilhelm Friedrich Ernst Bach. (given in prompt)
So the two links leave open whether Johann Ambrosius Bach is an ancestor of Wilhelm Friedrich Ernst Bach: yes, it could be that he is not.

notes: RBox revision (transitivity slot): ancestor_of (tagged transitive) is made intransitive (axiom not Trans); the paired contraction people-delete-0009 removes the same property. The statement says 'intransitive' so the negation question has no stacked 'not'; it is worded 'Is it true that the relation is not intransitive?'. Instances are real but minor lines whose end-to-end conclusion is hardly written: Erasmus Darwin to Gwen Raverat via Charles Darwin (17 Dolma co-occurrences of the two ends) and Johann Ambrosius Bach to Wilhelm Friedrich Ernst Bach via J. S. Bach. Yes and no: the first instance and the cross-lingual queries ask whether the conclusion follows (yes, then no), the second whether, given only the links, it could fail (no, then yes). Near asks transitivity of another people relation ('is older than'); far asks asymmetry of 'is heavier than'. hops counts the prompt's instance facts as one bridge (1 + 1).
